thread:
maddi: quick proposal — we should stop exporting raw request_id/prompt text out of the telemetry pipeline. idea: keep full values in the hot internal trace store for 24h, but for long-term retention export only deterministic, salted truncated hashes + low-cardinality buckets. thoughts?

aj: +1 on not exporting raw. what are we thinking for the hash function / truncation size? collisions are ok if we surface a bucket, but we need dedupe for alerts. :thinking:

chen: tradeoffs — truncated hashes work but we need consistent salt handling (rotation will scramble historical HLL/hyperloglog counts). two approaches: 1) HMAC with env-specific rotating salt + keep rotation window mapping, or 2) prefix-preserving fingerprint (harder). I lean HMAC(blake2b) -> hex[:16] + a ``prompt_bucket`` derived via low-bit entropy.

sasha: agree. also we should decide where scrubbing happens: ingest layer (shipper) vs exporter (observability pipeline). Doing it at ingest prevents any accidental export, but makes debugging harder. Doing it at exporter preserves full internal traces longer. ops-bot: ingest policy audit: current exporters send traces with request_id and user_id to datadog/obs. We can add a pipeline step to replace attributes before export.

maddi: proposal details: 
- keep raw request_id & prompt in internal traces for 24h only (hot store TTL).
- before exporting to long-term telemetry (retention >7d), replace request_id with HMAC(salt, id)[:16], store prompt_digest = BLAKE2b(prompt)[:12], and prompt_bucket = low_entropy(prompt_digest) (e.g., first 2 bytes) for low-cardinality dashboards.
- for alerting that needs de-duping, use the truncated hash. for sampling analytics use prompt_bucket + heuristic sampling.

aj: pseudocode looks ok. what about false positives for dedupe if truncated? collisions across tens of millions could be non-trivial. maybe use 24-bit instead of 16 hex chars?

chen: numbers: 16 hex chars =~ 64 bits? actually 16 hex chars = 64 bits? wait: 1 hex char = 4 bits so 16 chars = 64 bits, good. truncating to 12 chars = 48 bits. collision probability low for our scale. but if we *also* store prompt_bucket and timestamp bin, de-dupe should be fine.

sasha: operational concerns: dashboards that compute "unique user/request counts" via HyperLogLog need stable input. salt rotation breaks HLL estimates. options: 
- stop rotating salt frequently (rotate only on major security events), or
- attach salt_version to exported hashed value and maintain combined HLL across versions with correction, or
- run HLL on internal data before scrubbing and export HLL sketches only.

pm-oliver: from PM side — console customers expect unique counts and "Top failing prompts". we can't give raw prompts, but can we show "representative snippet" on demand with gating (audit log + auth) pulled from hot store? that's fine as long as retention is short and access is audited.

maddi: yes, that fits: short-lived hot store with controlled access for SRE/SEs, exported artifacts are hashed/bucketed. we'll add an "investigate" workflow that grabs raw context if authorized and within TTL.

aj: export vs ingest: leaning exporter-level scrub + an ingest kill-switch. reasons: we keep flexibility for internal debug, and exporters provide easier plugin points for third-party sinks. but we need a hard guard so no downstream exporter ever ships raw.

ops-bot: suggestion: implement a lint check in the exporter config repo that rejects any attribute mapping that contains raw attributes like "request_id", "user_email", "prompt_text" for long-term retention sinks. Also add a runtime sanitizer in the ingest path that zeroes those fields for external sinks.

chen: privacy note — for prompt hashing, avoid reversible hashing; use HMAC with secret salt stored in KMS. rotate per schedule but maintain mapping of salt_version -> validity window. include salt_version metadata on exported records.

maddi: sketch of attribute mapping we'll export: 
- request_id_hash: "hmac_v2:abcd1234..." 
- prompt_digest: "blake2b_v1:xyz..." 
- prompt_bucket: "pb_0x09" (low-cardinality)
- user_hash: "hmac_v2:..." (never export user_email or user_id raw)
- trace_id: keep for trace correlations internal only; external traces get trace_id_hash similarly

aj: autosampling idea: if a prompt_bucket is very high cardinality, automatically enable per-bucket sampling to keep telemetry cost bounded. plumb through a rate-limit header from API to ingestion so expensive clients can be throttled or sampled.

sasha: +1. we should also consider count-min sketch for approximate counts without storing identities (SMALL memory footprint) — helpful for per-route unique counts.

pm-oliver: UX question — rollouts/alerts: if we change hashing/truncation parameters, will alert thresholds change? we need an "alert migration" plan every time we modify hashing. prefer to lock hashing config for long periods.

chen: action: document hashing config & migration steps in eng-platform runbook. include a backfill plan: keep both old_hash and new_hash for 48h if we change salt, compute reconciliation metrics.

maddi: action items: 
- chen: flesh out HMAC + salt rotation + salt_version header (ETA: Tue)
- aj: prototype exporter sanitizer + lint rule (ETA: Wed)
- sasha: evaluate count-min sketch vs HLL for route counts and produce cost comparison (ETA: Fri)
- pm-oliver: spec "investigate workflow" and audit requirements (ETA: Thu)

maddi: TL;DR: keep raw in hot store short-term, export only salted truncated hashes + low-cardinality buckets, implement exporter lint + ingest guard, add gated investigate workflow. :+1:

pm-oliver: sounds good. happy to coordinate docs & product notes.

ops-bot: noted — will open tickets for exporter-lint (PLAT-4893) and ingest-sanitizer (PLAT-4894).

aj: quick question: do we want to hash prompts or also remove stopwords before hashing to reduce near-duplicates?

chen: maybe normalize: trim whitespace, lowercase, remove high-frequency stopwords and canonicalize variable tokens (UUIDs, emails) before hashing. but do this carefully to avoid changing semantics for debugging. we can make normalization configurable per route.

sasha: thanks all. small follow-up: include metrics on how many records are mutated by sanitizer (for telemetry on the scrubber). we should surface that to console so customers know how much data is redacted.

maddi: good call. I'll add a telemetry metric for "attributes_sanitized.count" and a per-sink breakdown.

maddi: end — if no objections I'll spin up the PRs today.

aj: no objections, go for it. :rocket:
